groups.text: It is currently 20 degrees and cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Sanctioned ships now make up 58 percent of tanker scrapping deals this year, as Western governments push to permanently remove blacklisted tonnage from circulation. Clarksons Research reports that 26 sanctioned vessels totaling 2.1 million deadweight tonnes have been sold for recycling so far in 2026, including 22 tankers. This trend persists even while overall demolition activity remains near historic lows due to strong freight conditions. In a different sphere of security, Microsoft is developing a patch for a Defender zero-day vulnerability called ShieldBreak. Disclosed by researcher Nightmare Eclipse, the flaw allows local attackers to gain system privileges on Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server systems. Meanwhile, in occupied Crimea, drone debris sparked a fire at the Yevpatoria Aircraft Repair Plant on the evening of August 16. Reports indicate three drones targeted antennas and transmitters at the western end of the runway at the military repair facility.

The war between Russia and Ukraine is moving closer to civilians on both sides. Ukraine recently launched one of its largest drone attacks against Russian territory, striking a Wildberries warehouse along with other sites. At the same time, Russian strikes have continued across Ukraine. These attacks are destroying industrial areas as well as civilian zones. The escalation shows a pattern of targeting infrastructure and non-military locations in both nations. This shift brings the direct violence of the conflict into more residential and commercial spaces.

President Donald Trump is moving to significantly scale back joint military exercises with South Korea, citing high costs and his personal relationship with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. While the current "Ulchi Freedom Shield" drills began this Monday as planned, Trump has instructed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to substantially reduce the scope of the maneuvers. The president argued on Truth Social that these exercises are not only expensive for the U.S., but send a signal toward North Korea that is totally inappropriate and hostile. He noted that North Korea remained respectful during his previous term and questioned whether such drills should continue in the future. These eleven-day exercises involve thousands of soldiers from both nations, though this year's schedule includes three fewer field exercises than last year. Amid these changes, Trump also linked his frustration with South Korea to the country's dealings with Iran.

Threat actors are exploiting a high-severity authentication flaw in macOS Screen Sharing to gain root access and deploy Monero cryptominers. The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-65400, allows remote attackers to log in simply by naming an account. Apple released fixes on August 6 for macOS Tahoe, Sequoia, and Sonoma, but the Dutch National Cyber Security Centrum warns that active abuse is occurring on systems with port 5900 accessible from the internet. Elsewhere in India, different tensions are emerging. In the Himalayan foothills of West Bengal, the Indian peafowl has shifted from a cultural icon to a nuisance for farmers. Because the bird is protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act, managing its thriving population involves heavy bureaucratic hurdles. Meanwhile, in Assam, Bal Raksha Bharat has opened a Child Friendly Space in Sivasagar's Nazira subdivision to provide psychosocial support for children affected by recent floods.

The Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has now become the deadliest in the country's history. Congolese authorities reported on Monday that the death toll has surpassed 2,300 people. This figure exceeds the losses seen during the previous major outbreak from 2018 to 2020. The current crisis is concentrated in the north and east of the country, where health infrastructure is poor and state presence remains fragile. These conditions have left the official response overwhelmed by a rapid explosion of cases. To combat the spread, several vaccines are currently being tested against this specific strain of the virus. The World Health Organization says it hopes to reverse the trend in the region within three months. For now, however, the situation remains critical as officials struggle to contain the virus in areas where medical resources are most depleted.

Hackers began exploiting a critical vulnerability in SAP Commerce Cloud just three days after its public disclosure. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-58231, involves insufficient authorization checks and input validation. With a maximum CVSS score of 10, the vulnerability allows attackers to execute arbitrary code and compromise internal components. While SAP released patches on August 11, threat intelligence organizations like Defused and KEVIntel confirmed exploitation attempts by August 14 and 15. In other news, Kenyan startup JentaHub has launched a verified talent marketplace to connect African professionals with global businesses, clients, and NGOs. Founder Joseph Ongachi started the self-funded venture this year to address rising unemployment among qualified Africans. He notes that while platforms like Upwork and Fiverr exist, a gap remains in helping African professionals overcome barriers to the digital economy and solving trust challenges for remote employers.

Violence has escalated along the border between Russia and Ukraine with a series of deadly strikes on both sides. In Russia's Belgorod region, acting governor Alexander Shuvaev reports that Ukrainian missile strikes killed six people overnight and injured four others, including a 14-year-old child. These attacks damaged a car and burned a building in the village of Koloskovo. Meanwhile, a drone strike targeting an industrial facility in Russia's southern Astrakhan region hit a home instead, killing one woman. Ukraine officials report their own losses from Russian drone strikes overnight in the Sumy region, where two people were killed. This follows a weekend of heavy casualties; Russian officials described a recent Ukrainian offensive as the largest scale of the year, while Russian attacks on Ukraine killed at least seven people and injured more than 39 this past Saturday night.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be cloudy with rain chances up to 75 percent and temperatures between 18 and 20 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.

On your calendar today: personal calendar: all day: Sommerferien 2026 Berlin, at 18:45, BLISS Reading Group at Merantix AI Campus, and at 19:00, AI Enthusiasts at c-base mainhall, AI Meetup at c-base, and ️ Twerchhau.
Mail worth checking: Amazon sent a shipping update for your order arriving tomorrow. Also, jiroo sent notifications regarding medication tracking and a payment receipt.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
